plain_english: Now the fourteenth chapter. The blessed Lord said: I will again declare the supreme, highest knowledge among knowledges, by knowing which all sages attained supreme siddhi. That very knowledge previously stated I will again speak with excellence, individually determining the nature of the gunas, in full detail. By 'having known which,' he declares the evident certainty and establishment of this knowledge.
sanskrit_cite: atha caturdaśo'dhyāyaḥ   śrībhagavānuvāca   paraṃ bhūyaḥ pravakṣyāmi jñānānāṃ jñānamuttamam | yajjñātvā munayaḥ sarve parāṃ siddhimito gatāḥ | yadeva pūrvoktaṃ jñānaṃ tadeva punaḥ prakarṣeṇa pratyekaṃ  guṇasvarūpanirūpaṇayā vaitatyena vakṣyāmi | yajjñātvā-ityanenāsya jñānasya dṛṣṭapratyayatāṃ prasiddhiṃ  cāha

plain_english: Having relied on this knowledge and attained sameness with me, they are not born even in creation, nor are they distressed in dissolution.
sanskrit_cite: idaṃ jñānamupāśritya mama sādharmyamāgatāḥ | sarge'pi  nopajāyante pralaye na vyathanti ca | vyathantīti-cchāndasatvāttiṅpratyayaḥ | evamanyatrāpi  suptiṅpratyaye vācyam | tatrādau saṃsṛtau kramamāha-

plain_english: My womb is the great Brahman; in it I place the seed; thence comes the birth of all beings, O Bhārata. For what is to be abandoned, once its cause is known, is easy — I, of unspeakable bliss-form, taking up my own expanding power as Brahman, my reflective power over beginningless atoms, set them transmigrating for grace.
sanskrit_cite: mama yonirmahadbrahma tasmingarbhaṃ dadāmyaham | sambhavaḥ  sarvabhūtānāṃ tato bhavati bhārata | hātavye jñāte tatkāraṇe ca sukaraṃ hi hānam | mama-tāvadavyapadeśyaparamānandarūpasya  mahadbramha-vṛṃhakātmīyaśaktirūpaṃ brahma | ātmīyāmeva hi  vimarśaśaktimālambyāhamanādīnātmāṇūn anugrahārthaṃ  saṃsārayāmi | ata eva-

plain_english: O son of Kunti, all forms arise in every womb; of them Brahman is the great womb, and I am the seed-giver and father. In all wombs, as primordial cause, the nourishing divine power whose nature is the vomiting-forth of all samsara is mother, and I am called father, possessor of power.
sanskrit_cite: sarvayoniṣu kaunteya mūrtayaḥ sambhavanti yāḥ | tāsāṃ brahma  mahadyonirahaṃ bījapradaḥ pitā | sarvāsu yoniṣu ādikāraṇatayā bṛṃhikā  bhagavacchāktiḥ-sakalasaṃsāravamanasvabhāvā mātā | pitā  tvahaṃ-śaktimānavyapadeśyaḥ

plain_english: The qualities sattva, rajas, and tamas, born of nature, bind the imperishable embodied self in the body; and this embodied one, identifying those guna-dharmas as self, is bound by them for enjoyment up to liberation.
sanskrit_cite: sattvaṃ rajastama iti guṇāḥ prakṛtisambhavāḥ | nibadhnanti  mahābāho dehe dehinamavyayam | dehī cāyamātmatayā sattvarajastamobhirdharmairapavargaparyantāya  bhogāya nibadhyeta

plain_english: There, sattva, being pure, illuminating, and free from disease, binds by attachment to pleasure and by attachment to knowledge, O sinless one.
sanskrit_cite: tatra sattvaṃ nirmalatvātprakāśakamanāmayam | sukhasaṅgena  badhnāti jñānasaṅgena cānagha

plain_english: Know rajas to be passion-natured, born of craving and attachment; that, O Kaunteya, binds the embodied one through attachment to action. In order, their form is said to be pure sattva, because craving is the origin of attachment.
sanskrit_cite: rajo rāgātmakaṃ viddhi tṛṣṇāsaṅgasamudbhavam | tannibadhnāti  kaunteya karmasaṅgena dehinam | krameṇaiṣāṃ rūpamucyate | sattvaṃ-nirmalam | tṛṣṇā saṅgasya  samudbhavo yataḥ

plain_english: Know that tamas, born of ignorance, deludes all embodied beings and binds them through negligence, laziness, and sleep. O Bharata, even rare human birth, gained by long-accumulated merit and the one cause of liberation, is wasted by negligence. Thus it is said: one moment of life cannot be obtained with all jewels; he who leads it vainly is negligent and the lowest man. Laziness in auspicious deeds is complete sleep, and sleep is a despised state.
sanskrit_cite: tamastvajñānajaṃ viddhi mohanaṃ sarvadehinām | pramādālasyanidrābhistannibadhnāni bhārata | durlabhasyāpi  ciratarasañcitapuṇyaśatalabdhasyāpavargaprāptāvekakāraṇasya  mānuṣyakasya vṛthātivāhanaṃ-pramādaḥ | tathāhyuktaṃ-   āyuṣaḥ kṣaṇa eko'pi sarvaratnairna labhyate | sa vṛthā nīyate  yena sa pramādī narādhamaḥ | iti | ālasyaṃ-śubhakaraṇīyeṣu | niḥśeṣeṇa drāṇam kutsitā  gatiḥ-nidrā

plain_english: O Bharata, sattva binds in happiness, rajas in action, and tamas, covering knowledge, binds in delusion.
sanskrit_cite: sattvaṃ sukhe sañjayati rajaḥ karmaṇi bhārata | jñānamāvṛtya tu  tamaḥ pramāde sañjayatyuta | sañjayati-yojayati

plain_english: O Bharata, when rajas and tamas are overcome, sattva becomes dominant; rajas overcomes sattva and tamas, and tamas overcomes sattva and rajas. Thus, when rajas and tamas are overcome, sattva increases; rajas overcomes sattva and tamas, and tamas overcomes sattva and rajas. It is said that the increase of a guṇa comes by mutual overcoming.
sanskrit_cite: rajastamaścābhibhūya sattvaṃ bhavati bhārata | rajaḥ sattvaṃ  tamaścaiva tamaḥ sattvaṃ rajastathā | rajastamasī abhibhūya sattvaṃ vardhate | rajastu sattvatamasī | tamaḥ sattvarajasī | uktaṃ hi anyonyābhibhavena guṇavṛddhiḥ | iti

plain_english: When knowledge arises as light in all the gates of this body, then know that sattva has increased.
sanskrit_cite: p. 288)   sarvadvāreṣu dehe'sminprakāśamupajāyate | jñānaṃ yadā tadā  vidyādvivṛddhaṃ sattvamityuta

plain_english: Greed, activity, restlessness in action, and thirst arise and grow when rajas predominates, O best of the Bharatas.
sanskrit_cite: lobhaḥ pravṛttirārambhaḥ karmaṇāmaśamaśca tṛṭ | rajasyetāni  jāyante vivṛddhe bharatarṣabha

plain_english: When tamas increases, darkness, inertia, delusion, and confusion arise; when rajas increases, greed and related qualities arise gradually through all the senses.
sanskrit_cite: aprakāśo'pravṛttiśca pramādo moha eva ca | tamasyetāni jāyante  vivṛddhe kurunandana | sarvadvāreṣu-sarvendriyeṣu | lobhādayaḥ krameṇaiva  rajasyudricyamāne jāyante | evamaprakāśādayaḥ krameṇaiva  tamovivṛddhāvāvirbhavanti

plain_english: When sattva increases, the embodied one goes to dissolution and attains pure worlds; through unbroken sattvic practice, increased sattva brings auspicious attainment.
sanskrit_cite: yadā sattve pravṛddhe tu pralayaṃ yāti dehabhṛt | tadottamavidāṃ  lokānamalānpratipadyate | yadā samagreṇaiva janmanānavaratasāttvikavyāpārābhyāsātsattvaṃ  vivṛddhaṃ bhavati tadā prāptapralayasya śubhalokāvāptiḥ

plain_english: Dissolution in rajas leads birth among action-bound beings; dissolution in tamas leads birth in deluded wombs; habitual tamas leads hell, animal, or tree births.
sanskrit_cite: rajasi pralayaṃ gatvā karmasaṅgiṣu jāyate | tathā pralīnastamasi  mūḍhayoniṣu jāyate | evaṃ janmābhyastarājasakarmaṇaḥ prayāṇāt vimiśropabhogāya  mānupyāvāptiḥ | tathā-tenaiva krameṇa yadā samagreṇa janmanā  tāmasameva karmābhyasyate tadā narakatiryagvṛkṣādideheṣūtpadyate | ye tu vyācakṣate-maraṇakāla eva sattvādau vivṛddhe etāni  phalāni-iti | te na samyakśārīre'nubhave praviṣṭāḥ | yataḥ  sarvasyaiva sarvathāntye kṣaṇe moha evopajāyate | asmadvyākhyāyāṃ ca saṃvādīnīmāni ślokāntarāṇi

plain_english: Good action yields pure sattvic fruit; rajas yields suffering and ignorance; tamas yields its own fruit.
sanskrit_cite: karmaṇaḥ sukṛtasyāhuḥ sāttvikaṃ nirmalaṃ phalam | rajasastu  phalaṃ duḥkhamajñānaṃ tamasaḥ phalam

plain_english: From sattva arises knowledge; from rajas arises greed, delusion, and confusion; from tamas arises ignorance.
sanskrit_cite: sattvātsañjāyate jñānaṃ rajaso lobha eva ca | pramādamohau  jāyete tamaso'jñānameva ca

plain_english: Those established in sattva go upward; rajas ones remain in the middle; tamas ones go downward.
sanskrit_cite: ūrdhvaṃ gacchanti sattvasthā madhye tiṣṭhanti rājasāḥ | jaghanyaguṇavṛttisthā adho gachanti tāmasāḥ

plain_english: When the seer sees no agent other than the strands and knows what is beyond them, he attains my nature.
sanskrit_cite: nānyaṃ guṇebhyaḥ kartāraṃ yadā draṣṭā'nupaśyati | guṇebhyaśca paraṃ vetti madbhāvaṃ so'dhigacchati

plain_english: Having transcended these three strands, the embodied one, freed from birth, death, old age, and suffering, tastes immortality.
sanskrit_cite: guṇānetānatītya trīndehī dehasamudbhavān | janmamṛtyujarāduḥkhairvimukto'mṛtamaśnute | atra kecidasaṃbaddhāḥ ślokāḥ kalpitāḥ punaruktatvātte tjājyā  eva | etadguṇātītavṛttistu mokṣāyaiva kalpate | nanu yadi ayaṃ dehī tatkathaṃ guṇātīto bhavati | sarvathaiva hi

plain_english: Arjuna asks by what signs, conduct, and means one transcends these three strands.
sanskrit_cite: kayāciccittavṛttyā vartate sā ca traiguṇyādanyatamā avaśyaṃ  bhavati ?-anenābhiprāyeṇa pṛcchati arjunaḥ   arjuna uvāca   kairliṅgaistrīnguṇānetānatīto bhavati prabho | kimācāraḥ  kathaṃ caitāṃstrīnguṇānativartate | atrottaraṃ-

plain_english: The Lord says one who neither hates illumination, activity, and delusion nor desires their arising or cessation becomes strand-transcending.
sanskrit_cite: śībhagavānuvāca   prakāśaṃ ca pravṛttiṃ ca mohameva ca pāṇḍava | na dveṣṭi  sampravṛttāni na nivṛttāni kāṅkṣati | yadyapi prakāśādikāḥ sarveṣu dharmeṣu vartante tathāpi  yoginasteṣu prakāśādiṣu na rajyante nāpi dveṣavanto bhavanti | apitu kevalapiṇḍadharmatayaite sthitāḥ na māṃ kṣobhayitumalam-iti  manvānā guṇātītā bhavanti | ata evāha-

plain_english: Seated like an indifferent one, not shaken by the strands, knowing they operate, the unwise stands and does not move.
sanskrit_cite: udāsīnavadāsīno guṇairyo na vicālyate | guṇā vartante ityeva  yo'jñastiṣṭhati neṅgate

plain_english: Equal in pain and pleasure, in clod, stone, and gold, in pleasant and unpleasant, the steady one is equal in blame and self-praise.
sanskrit_cite: samaduḥkhasukhaḥsvapnaḥ samaloṣṭāśmakāñcanaḥ | tulyapriyāpriyo dhīrastulyanindātmasaṃstutiḥ

plain_english: He who is equal in honor and dishonor, friend and foe, abandoning fruits of all undertakings, is called beyond the strands; though appearing ignorant, he stands without discrimination, and from right knowing he does not fall from his own form.
sanskrit_cite: mānāvamānayostulyastulyo mitrāparipakṣayoḥ | sarvārambhaphalatyāgī guṇātītaḥ sa ucyate | yaḥ ajño nirvivekastiṣṭhati sa eva jñaḥ-samyagjñānāt | tathā  hi | neṅgate-na svarūpāccyavate | atra  copāyaḥ-śarīrendriyādisvabhāva eṣa yatpravartanam natu phalaṃ  kiṃcidahamabhisandadha iti sthirā buddhiḥ

plain_english: Who serves me with unwavering devotion-yoga transcends these strands and becomes fit for brahman-becoming; this is the root means taught, and the one who serves me alone without desiring fruit is purified by the Lord's foremost power.
sanskrit_cite: māṃ ca yo'vyabhicāreṇa bhaktiyogena sevate | sa  guṇānsamatītyaitānbrahmabhūyāya kalpate | anena mūlabhūtamupāyamupadiśati māṃ ceti | caśabdo'vadhāraṇe  yo māmeva sevate | anena-phalādisākāṅkṣo māmaṅgatvenā śrayati  phalaṃ pradhānatayā-iti nirantaḥ | ata eva nāsyāvyabhicāriṇī  maktiḥ-phalaṃ prati hyasāvāsthāvāniti | yastu phalaṃ  kiṃcidapyanabhilaṣyan kimetadalīkamanutiṣṭhasi-iti  paryanuyujyamāno'pi  nirantarabhagavadbhaktivedhavidrutāntaḥkaraṇatayā  kaṇṭakitaromavān  vepamānatanurvisphāritanayanayugalaparivartamānasalilasaṃpātaḥ  tūṣṇīṃbhāvenaivottaraṃ prayacchati | sa evāvyabhicāriṇyā  bhagavato maheśvarasyāgraśaktyā bhaktyā pavitrīkṛto nānya iti  jñeyam

plain_english: I am the foundation of brahman, the immortal and imperishable, and of eternal duty and absolute happiness; when I am served, brahman becomes, otherwise worshipped brahman remains inert and would give liberation no different from deep sleep.
sanskrit_cite: brahmaṇo hi pratiṣṭhāhamamṛtasyāvyayasya ca | śāśvatasya ca  dharmasya sukhasyaikāntikasya ca | ahameva hi brahmaṇaḥ pratiṣṭhā | mayi sevyamāne brahma bhavati  anyathā jaḍarūpatayā brahma upāsyamānaṃ mokṣamapi  sauṣuptādaviśiṣṭameva prāpayediti śivam

plain_english: Here is the summary verse: shining with devotion-rasa absorption and free from ego-delusion, even when strands conflict, the guṇa-transcendent ascetic remains equal.
sanskrit_cite: atra saṃgrahaślokaḥ   lasadbhaktirasāveśahīnāhaṃkāravibhramaḥ | sthite'pi  guṇasaṃmarde guṇātītaḥ samo yatiḥ | iti śrīmahāmaheśvarācāryavaryarājānakābhinavaguptapādaviracite  śrīmadbhagavadgītārthasaṃgrahe caturdaśo'dhyāyaḥ
